surfaces.part: snow ramp slope with rock edges

answer.evidence: Rows 0-14 are a lighter sloped snow plane (L=210). It narrows into a V at rows 8-13 and has rocks with dark outlines on both sides. The dark rock base at row 14 acts as the front edge. Rows 15-31 are a flat, speckled cliff face (L=180) 17 rows tall, so there is a clear front face below the sloped top. The edge line is weak and the ramp is only suggested by the V shape, so this is a moderate-confidence three_quarter reading rather than a clear one.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's ramp surface is a large pale, near-uniform fill with only a faint soft gradient and a few dark triangular wall-edge shapes at the top corners. Near-flat coverage is 50%, while both references are at 0%. The surface has no snow grain, speckle or per-patch highlights, which the references carry through grass tufts and shaded paving stones. The measured 11 visible tones per tile beat the references, but they appear to be concentrated in the corner shapes and edges rather than spread across the surface. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline is tinted and not a sticker line. The ramp itself has about 3 lightness steps against roughly 5-6 in the references. Large flat areas and thin texture make it look flatter than the references, so it fails.
